name: Trail Trainer
author: Dandyhorse
description: Real routes, ridden as they are. The shape and the climbing come from open map and elevation data; the scenery is drawn from it. Routes take hours, so stop whenever you like and pick up where you left off.

first-session.name: Out the door
first-session.description: Rode part of a real route.

resumed.name: Where you left it
resumed.description: Picked a route up part-way through.

summit.name: The whole climb
summit.description: Rode Alpe d'Huez end to end.

end-to-end.name: End to end
end-to-end.description: Finished a route, however many sessions it took.

variants.name: Trail Trainer (Bike)
variants.description: Your measured power moves the bike against the real gradient, and the trainer holds it. Stop pedalling and you coast.

variants.name: Trail Trainer (Run)
variants.description: The belt speed you choose is your speed on the trail; the game sets the incline from the route. No coasting — you run every metre.

route.label: Route
route.description: Which real route to ride. You keep your place on each one separately.

others.label: Other people
others.description: How many other riders and walkers are out. Each one is a full avatar; turn them off on a weak GPU.

shadows.description: Sun shadows near the rider. Turn off on a weak GPU.

viewDistance.description: How much of the landscape is drawn. 'Far' shows the other side of the valley on mountain routes.

notes.saveState: Progress is a position per route, not a score: { routes: { <id>: { s, elapsed, sessions, completed } } }. A session that ends part-way along a route is a success, not an abandonment — see INTEGRATION.md §5.
notes.duration: requestedDuration ends the session, not the route. Routes are hours or days long by design.
